pending.text: Most PEFT papers benchmark accuracy gains. This one measures what you lose: pretrained knowledge retention under the stability-plasticity lens. Turns out the "efficient" part sometimes means silently erasing what the model already knew. http://arxiv.org/abs/2605.28819v1

The real bottleneck isn't simulation fidelity: it's that we keep compressing touch into a caricature to cross the gap. This paper treats contact as a physics-grounded representation rather than a crude signal. That changes what sim-to-real can preserve.

The interesting thing about this paper is that it treats CLIP's matching as two separable stages: extracting attributes from images and aggregating them for classification. http://arxiv.org/abs/2605.28809v1
